claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a near-random, homogeneous atomic distribution with minimal short-range order.
A modestly elevated thermal pre-treatment can induce additional short-range ordering in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The induced short-range ordering increases local lattice distortion.
Increased local lattice distortion produces greater variability in surface atomic coordination environments.
Increased local lattice distortion broadens the distribution of adsorption-site binding energies.
The altered adsorption-energy distribution weakens the binding of carbonaceous ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Overly strong binding of carbonaceous intermediates promotes accumulation of coke precursors that deactivate active sites.
Weakening carbonaceous-intermediate binding reduces catalyst poisoning and improves durability during ethanol oxidation.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the thermally pre-treated catalyst will accumulate carbon deposits more slowly.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the thermally pre-treated catalyst will sustain higher catalytic activity, including higher turnover frequency and lower deactivation rate.
The untreated catalyst has a more homogeneous atomic arrangement and less lattice distortion than the thermally pre-treated catalyst.
The proposed mechanism applies during ethanol oxidation at approximately 70–120 °C and ambient pressure in a typical electrochemical reactor.
The hypothesis is limited to pre-treatments that do not cause phase segregation or significant composition changes.
Untreated and thermally pre-treated PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts should be compared under otherwise identical ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Carbon accumulation, catalytic activity over time, local lattice distortion, and phase homogeneity can be measured to test the proposed causal chain.
Failure of the pre-treated catalyst to show a statistically significant reduction in carbon buildup or improved activity retention relative to the untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
